operator_io_quirks: Table name "transaction" is a SQL keyword and is quoted in DDL; generated SQL must double-quote it.
location<->geolocation form a 2-cycle of FKs on LocationID (each references the other); process_order must break the cycle deterministically.
rootbeer.LocationID has TWO FK entries to different parents (location and geolocation) on the same column; fks dict keyed by (child_t,child_c) can hold only one - the second is lost.
rootbeerreview has composite PK (CustomerID, BrandID); both members are also FKs to different parents.
geolocation and location each have only 3 rows; rootbeer/transaction have 6k+ rows - FK child draws from a 3-value parent give heavy ties.
DATE columns (FirstPurchaseDate, PurchaseDate, ReviewDate, TransactionDate) are stored as TEXT 'YYYY-MM-DD'; declared DATE dispatches to Date fuzzer (first element not int).
FirstBrewedYear is INTEGER holding years 1898-1986; declared INTEGER -> Number fuzzer, not Year (no 'year' in type string).
ZipCode INTEGER holds 5-digit codes (94256...); Number fuzzer will produce small ints, not zip-like values.
CreditCardNumber INTEGER holds 16-digit values (6011583832864739); Number fuzzer range is +-10^scale, far smaller.

Boolean-ish TEXT columns (SubscribedToEmailList, CaneSugar, CornSyrup, Honey, ArtificialSweetener, Caffeinated, Alcoholic, AvailableInCans/Bottles/Kegs) store 'TRUE'/'FALSE' strings; declared TEXT -> String fuzzer, not Bool.
High-null columns: rootbeerreview.Review 0.978, rootbeerbrand.Twitter 0.917, FacebookPage 0.75, Website 0.083; location text cols 0.333.
No NOT NULL constraints anywhere (all notnull=0); PKs are INTEGER primary key (rowid alias) so NULL PKs become auto-assigned rowids on insert.
operator_ts_expectations: Date fuzzer with template %Y-%m-%d on the four DATE columns; range from min/max of 5 sampled originals (e.g. 2013-2016), so fresh dates stay in that window.
String fuzzer for names/cities/emails/phones/URLs: random a-zA-Z0-9() strings, not plausible emails/phones/URLs -> FN on LIKE '%@%', phone-format, URL-prefix predicates.
Number fuzzer on ZipCode/CreditCardNumber/FirstBrewedYear: small ints in +-10^scale, so range predicates like ZipCode BETWEEN 90000 AND 96000 or year>1900 mostly miss -> FN.
Boolean TEXT columns get random strings, not 'TRUE'/'FALSE' -> predicates = 'TRUE' or IN ('TRUE','FALSE') become near-empty -> FN.
State has distinct=1 ('CA') in customers; String fuzzer will emit many other values -> predicates State='CA' still match some rows but joins on State become noisy.
geolocation/location have 3 rows; FK draws from 3 values produce massive duplicate LocationID in rootbeer/transaction -> joins explode, COUNT(*) predicates differ from original -> FP.
rootbeerreview composite PK (CustomerID,BrandID) with FK draws from 554x24 parents: PK dedup keeps first occurrence, so review counts per brand collapse -> COUNT/HAVING predicates miss -> FN.
rootbeer.LocationID FK to two parents: only one edge survives in fks dict, so half the join semantics (geolocation vs location) may be inconsistent -> FP on joins to the dropped parent.
StarRating INTEGER 1-5: Number fuzzer range +-10^scale (scale 0 -> +-1) plus perturbation, so ratings cluster near 0/1/2 -> AVG(StarRating) and rating>=4 predicates miss -> FN.
PurchasePrice/WholesaleCost/CurrentRetailPrice REAL: Number fuzzer with scale 0 gives ints in +-1, so price comparisons (price>3) mostly false -> FN.
No NOT NULL: TS may insert NULLs into PK columns; INTEGER PRIMARY KEY auto-assigns rowid, so PK uniqueness holds but values differ from original ranges -> join/range predicates on IDs miss.
